source.title: Vorticity and Regularity for Viscous Incompressible Flows under the Dirichlet Boundary Condition. Results and Related Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Consider a weak solution u of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations in the half-space Ω = R^3_+ with the non-slip (Dirichlet) boundary condition u|∂Ω = 0. Let ω(x,t) = ∇×u(x,t) be the vorticity, and let θ(x,y,t) denote the angle between the vorticities at two points x and y at time t. In the region where |ω(x,t)| and |ω(y,t)| are both larger than a fixed positive constant K, is it sufficient for regularity that the vorticity directions satisfy the 1/2-Hölder coherence condition sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x−y|^(1/2) for almost every t? Is even the stronger Lipschitz coherence condition sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x−y| sufficient?

evidence.quote: Open Problem. Consider the problem (2.1), (2.12) with Ω = R3+ . Is the assumption (2.4) (or even(2.2)) sufficient to guarantee the regularity of the solution?

accepted.question_text: For the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations, can the regularity criteria based on geometric control of the vorticity direction that are known in the whole space, and partly known for slip boundary conditions, be extended to boundary value problems?
accepted.context_brief: Extension of vorticity-direction regularity theory to boundaries

evidence.quote: A main open problem is the extension of the above type of results to boundary value problems.
Another central problem is the extension of the basic theory to boundary value problems.

accepted.question_text: Consider weak solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations in the half-space Ω = R^3_+ under the slip boundary condition u_3 = 0 and ∂u_j/∂x_3 = 0 for 1 ≤ j ≤ 2. Suppose that in the region where the vorticity at both points is larger than a fixed positive constant K one has the coherence estimate sin θ(x,y,t) ≤ c|x−y|^β, where θ(x,y,t) is the angle between the vorticities at x and y and β lies in [0, 1/2]. What is the smallest exponent β for which this geometric assumption alone, without additional hypotheses such as ω ∈ L^2(0,T;L^r), is sufficient to guarantee regularity? In particular, can the threshold be improved below β = 1/2?
accepted.context_brief: Best Hölder exponent for slip-boundary regularity

evidence.quote: The central and more challenging open problem is the improvement of the best exponent β for which the assumption (2.9) guarantees the regularity of the solutions without any other additional hypotheses.
